Hi Dana —

Thanks for the detailed numbers and the sheet — super helpful. High level answers first, then a short note on tradeoffs:

1) Baseline Dedicated pool recommendation: 4 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (locked to a 32k-optimized model variant) for sustained throughput, with ability to burst to +50% (e.g., 6x) for predictable peak windows. That assumes continuous batching and prefix/KV cache for the research assistant.

2) Hedging factor: plan for ~1.4x headroom compared to average-to-peak QPS to account for burstiness and cache-warmup. This is driven by your 30% long-context traffic which increases per-request memory by ~2.5–3x.

3) Quantization: for the 32k research model we recommend starting with an 8-bit QAT (or PG-GM 8-bit recipe) for most traffic and reserve an FP16 or BF16 variant for strict SLAs on latency-sensitive queries. 4-bit (INT4) can yield big cost savings but needs rigorous evals on hallucination/regression — we can run our Optimize eval harness on your prompt set.

I'll loop Marissa & Marcus on sizing details (memory breakdown, KV cache assumptions, expected tail latency). Also attaching our Dedicated pricing draft for reference.

Next steps: can we set a quick internal call tomorrow so we can give a precise GPU count by model variant?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Jordan / Marcus —

Quick calc below. Assumptions are conservative; I'll add notes where I relaxed constraints.

Assumptions:
- Model sizes: 32k variant = 70B params (~140GB FP16 weights), 16k variant = 35B params (~70GB FP16).
- KV cache scale roughly ~0.6 bytes/token stored per token in KV (post-quantization affects this).
- Average long-context request stores ~24k tokens in KV during inference (prompt + intermediate).

Per-GPU resident memory (ballpark)
- FP16 (32k model): weights pinned across 2 GPUs (sharded): ~70GB/GPU + KV buffer per active request. Concurrent contexts per GPU depends on batching.
- 8-bit (Q8) reduces weights footprint ~1.9x: ~37GB/GPU equivalent. KV storage also compresses ~1.8x in our pipeline.
- 4-bit (Q4) reduces weights ~3.3x but increases kernel overhead and can inflate tail latency by ~20–40% for long-context runs unless kernel fusion is tuned.

Capacity sketch for ApexGen traffic (conservative headroom):
- Start: 3 x 80GB-class GPUs dedicated to the 32k variant (Q8) serving 75 rpm long-context with continuous batching and a hot KV prefix cache. This gives ~1.3x headroom.
- Add: 2 x 80GB-class GPUs for the 16k summarization pool (Q8) with autoscale triggers at 65% utilization and burst to +1 GPU for 15-minute windows.
- Burst policy: allow borrowing of spare capacity between pools (same AZ preference) — enable canary spillover to FP16 variant for latency-critical queries.

Estimated cost delta (hourly serving cost normalized):
- FP16 baseline: 1.0x
- Q8: ~0.55–0.6x cost vs FP16 (memory + throughput savings)
- Q4: ~0.35–0.45x but expect 15–40% higher p95 latency for long-context unless using tuned kernels and additional headroom.

Operational asks:
- We should run Redwood Optimize evals on their prompt subset before committing to Q4 for the 32k model.
- Add a canary route that funnels 5–10% of traffic to FP16 variant for latency-sensitive customers.

I'll draft the numbers into a short slide and we can send a recommendation back to Dana. Marcus, anything to add on autoscale behavior or pool tiling?

—Marissa

Adding a few operational points that change the recommendation slightly:

1) KV cache warmup: if prefix reuse is low at launch, expect initial burst memory pressure — bump initial 32k pool to 4 x 80GB-class GPUs for the first 2 weeks and re-evaluate after we collect real cache hit rates.
2) Model variants: serve Q8 as default. Maintain a small FP16 staging pool (1 GPU) as a fallback to meet strict p95 SLOs; route via smart-routing policy when latency > threshold.
3) Autoscale and billing: recommend reserved capacity for the baseline pool and on-demand burst to avoid committing for uncertain peak windows. That gives ApexGen the best mix of cost predictability and operational safety.

I can take the numbers and produce a recommended Dedicated order: 4x reserved 80GB + burst to 2x on-demand for 90-day initial term.

—Marcus
